rationale: Eavor qualifies geographically as a Calgary-headquartered Canadian company, but it fails the direct-infrastructure business and mandate tests. Eavor expressly describes a capital-light model centered on licensing proprietary geothermal technology and supplying engineering, construction and operating services, with selective project equity. Geretsried is a separate multi-sponsor build-own-operate SPV in Germany; Eavor and Enex together hold only an approximately 30% interest, and no Temasek project-SPV interest or infrastructure mandate is disclosed. Temasek's 2021 corporate financing and 2023 follow-on are therefore out-of-scope technology/growth investments.
recommendedChanges: Exclude Eavor Technologies Inc. from Temasek's North American direct infrastructure-equity PortCo census.
Retire the repository's active Temasek ownership period at list level through an exclusion proposal rather than representing Temasek as sole owner.
Preserve the 2021 Temasek entry and 2023 follow-on as out-of-scope climate-technology financing history.
Keep Eavor GmbH and Eavor Erdwärme Geretsried GmbH & Co. KG beneath Eavor; do not create Geretsried as a Temasek PortCo.
Do not infer Eavor's standalone Geretsried percentage from the disclosed approximately 30% combined Eavor/Enex interest.
unresolvedQuestions: Temasek's continuing ownership at the cutoff date is not publicly resolved.
Temasek's investing entity, security, stake, governance rights and 2023 follow-on amount are not publicly disclosed.
The Eavor/Enex split and Eavor's audited licensing/services versus project cash-flow mix are not publicly disclosed.
